title: Evidence
description: A first-class, pinned, reproducible proof object. Every claim in the estate must resolve to one of these. Evidence is never re-derived — it is only extended or superseded.

claim_id.description: Unique, stable identifier. Format: <domain>.<slug> e.g. sched.stale-worker-fencing

claim.description: Plain-language statement of the property being verified. Must be falsifiable.

status.description: STALE = source_head has drifted beyond staleness_threshold. SUPERSEDED = replaced by a newer claim_id.

mechanism.description: The technical mechanism that makes this claim true. e.g. generation_fenced_leases

implementation.description: Pinned file:line-range references. Must be stable at source_head.

verification.description: Test files or scripts that demonstrate the claim is true

commands.description: Exact commands to reproduce verification from a clean checkout at source_head

measured_results.description: Quantitative benchmark output. null if claim is correctness-only.

limitations.description: Known conditions under which the claim does NOT hold. Intellectual honesty is required here.

source_head.description: PINNED commit SHA at which verification was performed. Never a branch name. This is what makes evidence permanently reproducible.

verified_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of last successful verification

verified_by.description: Agent or operator that ran verification. e.g. github-actions/ci, operator/casey

staleness_threshold_days.description: After this many days without re-verification, status auto-transitions to STALE. Default 90.

superseded_by.description: claim_id of the Evidence object that replaces this one. Only set when status=SUPERSEDED.

engineering_run_id.description: References the engineering-run that produced this evidence

tags.description: Free-form labels for cross-cutting queries. e.g. concurrency, distributed-systems, resume-worthy
